questions.question: On a frontal chest radiograph, which sign is characteristic of left atrial enlargement?
questions.detail: The double density sign occurs when the right border of the enlarged left atrium is seen through the right atrium.

questions.question: Which congenital heart lesion classically presents with a 'boot-shaped' heart (coeur en sabot) on plain film?
questions.detail: Right ventricular hypertrophy in TOF uplifts the cardiac apex, creating the classic boot-shaped appearance.

questions.question: Massive right atrial enlargement is a hallmark of which cyanotic heart lesion on chest radiography?
questions.detail: Ebstein anomaly features severe tricuspid regurgitation and a 'box-shaped' heart due to massive RA enlargement.

questions.question: A 'narrow superior mediastinum' and an enlarged heart create the 'egg-on-a-string' appearance characteristic of:
questions.detail: The 'string' represents the narrow mediastinal waist caused by the parallel orientation of the great vessels and thymic stress.

questions.question: Pulmonary vascularity is typically DECREASED on a chest radiograph in which of the following conditions?
questions.detail: TOF involves RV outflow tract obstruction, leading to reduced pulmonary blood flow and 'clear' (oligemic) lungs.
